note: Vol. I No. 48. The town is on page 3. This issue completes the fire ordinance begun on 1834-10-01 — the trustees met at the Tremont House on 13 October and gave the wardens command at a fire, in force from 25 October — and it carries no Chicago letter list, only the Hennepin and Plainfield ones, which are recorded and not minted.

claims.notes: THE TRUSTEES MET AT THE TREMONT HOUSE ON 13 OCTOBER 1834, and this ordinance gives the fire wardens appointed on 20 September the power to command any bystander at a fire into the bucket line. It is the second half of the ordinance of 1834-10-01 and settles that one's date: 'the Ordinance dated the 20th day of September A. D. 1834' is the same sitting the earlier notice describes at the Presbyterian church. The meeting place is read as the Tremont House from 'the Tre.' plus the ordinance of 29 September, which prints 'ot House' at the same point. claims.normalized: Fashionable Tailoring. [Th]e [s]ubscriber[s] beg leave to [inform the citi]zens of Chicago and it[s] vicinity, that [the]y have commence[d] the Tailoring business in [i]ts various branches, [nor]th of [the Tremo]nt House, Having had a[n] ex[p]erimental […] in [… their] art, [they flat]ter themselves to be inferior to none, and [ho]pe by a strict attention to their business to [me]rit a share of public patronage. ANDREWS & EELLS, Chicago, Oct. 22, 18[34].
claims.notes: A PARTNERSHIP FORMED INSIDE THIS MONTH. Thomas S. Eels advertises the tailoring business alone in the issue of 1834-10-01 under a July dateline and with no address; here, dated 22 October 1834, it is ANDREWS & EELLS and it has one — north of the Tremont House. Both notices stand with their dates and neither overwrites the other; no identity merge is declared between 'Thomas S. Eels' and the firm, because a man and a firm are not the same record. The offset word is cut to '«1 eth of Tree}' and is read as 'north of the Tremont' from the run's other uses of that anchor; it is bracketed, and the placement stands on the anchor rather than on the direction.

claims.notes: A TRADE THE TOWN HAD AND THE RECONSTRUCTION DOES NOT: silver ornaments made for the Indian trade, wanted by a Chicago jeweller in the same month the last treaty payment was being made. The advertiser is the watchmaker who advertises for a journeyman in the issue of 1834-10-01 as 'It. MULFORD' and 'I. MULFORD'; the initial is single-witness in every printing and is bracketed as uncertain rather than resolved, so no person is minted.

claims.notes: NOT A CHICAGO LIST. This issue carries the Hennepin and P[l]ainfield lists and no Chicago one, and their names are deliberately NOT minted: ruling 1 mints a resident CANDIDATE off the Chicago post office's list, and a letter waiting at Hennepin says nothing about who lived in Chicago. Recorded so the reading's boundary is on the record rather than implied by an absence. The place name is cut to 'Hen' and read as Hennepin from the run.
